..
While a generally dry period remains through the weekend,
precipitable water remains between 1.75" and 2.25" across all
islands. This moisture is expected to remain along with light and
variable winds, so island effect showers and isolated thunderstorms 
will be possible Saturday, Sunday, and Monday. The highest chances
will be for Guam. Light northwesterlies Saturday across Guam may 
keep showers more to the southeast. While no thunderstorms were
observed over the islands today, upper-level support looks to 
increase slightly the next three days which should help support 
thunderstorm development. By Tuesday, westerlies winds ahead of a 
slowly developing trough will prevent further island effect showers, 
but then bring additional monsoon moisture into the region by 
Wednesday. This will bring shower coverage back to scattered with 
isolated thunderstorms possible. This trough will be closely 
monitored for any potential impacts to the Marianas late next week.

Marine...
Light to variable winds will prevail through the weekend. Seas 
around 3 feet will remain small until at least Tuesday before 
possibly starting to increase. Swells currently consist of a very
small southwest swell and an east-northeast swell. The risk of rip 
currents is currently low along all reefs of the Marianas and is 
expected to stay that way through at least Tuesday. Isolated 
thunderstorms could drift over the waters during afternoon island 
effect convection for the next three days. This will cause a moderate
risk of lightning in the afternoon along the coastlines.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Storm Surigae (25W) is centered east-northeast of Luzon, 
Philippines near 20.2N 130.3E. Surigae is moving northwest at 13 
mph. Surigae remains a tropical storm, with maximum sustained winds 
of 45 mph. Tropical storm force winds are found only in the northern
half of Surigae. TS Surigae will make a gradual turn toward the 
northwest, then north, over the next couple of days, eventually 
turning northeast around Sunday night or Monday. It is expected to 
move out of the Guam Area of Responsibility (AOR) within the next 6 
to 12 hours. Surigae is expected to strengthen a bit over the next 
few days as well, possibly becoming a typhoon Saturday night or 
Sunday morning.

For more information on TS Surigae, please see bulletins issued by
the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and 
from the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
A band of convergence south of the monsoon trough, within the 
monsoon flow, will maintain scattered showers and isolated
thunderstorms across Pohnpei and Kosrae for the next couple of days.
This convergence will continue to slowly decrease, allowing a drier 
pattern to move into Pohnpei and Kosrae late in the weekend, 
continuing dry through the middle of next week. For Majuro, the dry
pattern currently in place will slowly erode through the evening,
with showers and thunderstorms seen to the east of the atoll moving
into the region later tonight, near midnight. Latest guidance keeps
an active pattern across the Marshalls through the weekend and into
next week as the eastern end of the monsoon trough remains over the
area and weak surface trough traverse the boundary.

For the marine forecast, no big changes were made to the inherited 
forecast. Mostly light to gentle winds will prevail through the 
middle of next week, though Pohnpei can expect occasional moderate 
winds for the next couple of days. Benign seas will continue for the
next several days.

Western Micronesia...
Numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms are expected to persist 
at Yap through the weekend as a moist, west to southwest monsoonal 
flow lingers across the area, before it slowly lifts northward over 
the next couple of days. Locally heavy showers are still possible 
for Yap, but confidence remains low. Mostly isolated to low-end 
scattered showers are expected to continue at Palau through Saturday 
night before drier conditions settle in this weekend. Unsettled 
weather is developing to the southwest of Chuuk and is expected to 
fill over the evening and overnight hours. This will bring numerous 
showers and isolated thunderstorms forecast to continue through 
Saturday night. Gentle to moderate west to southwest winds will 
continue at all sites for the next couple of days with winds easing 
slightly this weekend for Palau and Yap. Generally benign marine 
conditions are expected to prevail through at least the weekend with 
combined seas of 3 to 5 feet expected at all forecast points. Though,
locally choppy seas will be possible near Yap and Chuuk with heavier
showers and thunderstorms.
